There is an extensive literature on searches for the supersymmetric Higgs bosons of the Model Supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model (MSSM) at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). Much of this literature has focussed on the case where the lightest MSSM Higgs boson, often called h, is the only Higgs boson below the fcompleted MSSM particle pair. In this case, the h may decay into almost any standard model (SM) particle pair and may have substantial coupling to bottom quarks and Z bosons. Therefore, h may be discovered at the LHC through its standard model like decays into jets, W bosons and Z bosons, along with some evidence of a new state, often called the singlet Higgs boson, S, that can escape detection in the dijet mass spectrum arising from the cascade decay h->S+S. Such a discovery may be very compelling evidence for the MSSM, but this general search strategy will be challenging to implement at the LHC if the next lightest supersymmetric Higgs boson, often called HNH, has substantial coupling to bottom quarks and is heavier than approximately 900 GeV. If the HNH is not too heavy, then it will typically decay both into a bottom quark and a neutralino, which gives rise to a very different final state than the one arising from the cascade decays of h. The HNH branching fraction to jets will be small, so that discovery and characterization of this state will likely require very large data samples and sophisticated multivariate analysis techniques. A direct search for the HNH via this approach is unlikely at the LHC, but may be promising at a future circular hadron collider.

Nanographenes are carbon nanostructures with a sp2 hybridized carbon ring and are consisting of carbon and aromatic rings. These nanostructures show many interesting physical properties such as semiconducting behavior, superconductivity, nonlinear optics and many more. Magnetism is one of the physical properties that has been observed in nanographenes. In this paper, we have performed first principles study of magnetism in nanographenes. We have investigated two nanographenes with different ring numbers and different positive and negative charges. Our results show that in case of neutral nanographene with even number of rings, there is anti-ferromagnetic interaction between neighboring rings. But for the case of the positively charged nanographene with odd number of rings, there is ferromagnetic interaction between neighboring rings. The estimated magnetic moments for neutral and positively charged nanographenes are 2.2μB and 4.2μB respectively.

In this paper we present a quasi-linear time algorithm for computing modular polynomials. Let f be a monic, positive definite polynomials with integer coefficients. The modular polynomial associated to f is defined as where χ(n) is the principle thueist getting all roots of unity as n runs over the positive integers. Computing the modular polynomial for a given modulus M is fundamental in number theory and its application is well known. In the case of number theory it arises when computing Shafarevich–Tate groups and for that purpose a modular polynomial with certain properties is needed. The task of computing the modular polynomial associated to a given polynomial is known to be hard and it has been shown that it cannot be approximated within a factor of n^c for any c < 1 unless thepolynomial evaluation problem is hardness for c=1. We present a quasi-linear time algorithm for computing modular polynomials. It follows from a simpler algorithm for computing prime factors of moduli and for that purpose we prove some hardness results about the modular polynomial. Our algorithm has application in computing Shafarevich–Tate groups and it would be interesting to see if it can be used to improve the best known algorithm for this problem.

The paper introduces the formalism to classify N=8 supergravity theories in five distinctive families and presents their space-time vector fields content. It begins by reviewing the structure of N=8 supergravity theories and the embedding of its maximal SU(8) bosonic subgroup in the N=8 supersymmetric Poincaré group. Next, it describes a systematic classification of these theories in five distinct families. The first family consists of the so-called maximally extended theories, which contains all N=8 supergravity theories as well as their consistent toroidal truncations. The second family consists of theories with SO(p, 1) invariance, which are based on the coset space G/H where G is the hidden symmetry group of maximal supergravity and H is one of its subgroup. The third family of theories is based on the supergroup E$_{7(7)}/$SU(8). The fourth family is based on the SO(p, 4) x SO(7−p) symmetry, where p is the number of space-time vector fields. The last family contains theories with SO(p, 3, C) symmetry, where C denotes the reality of the N=8 C Becfore brane.

LANS-alpha model is a common dimensional reduction technique to simulate flows with high Reynolds numbers. A reduced order model is constructed by projecting high dimensional flow equations onto a lower dimensional subspaces which are then used as input sets to the flow equations. This method works well when the reduced order model solutions are highly turbulent in nature. In this paper, we present such highly turbulent solutions for LANS-alpha model and their LES counterpart. The results are presented for flows with Reynolds numbers of a cylinder at a fixed inclination angle. The solutions are solved using a spectral method which discretises the LANS-alpha and LES models in spectral space using non-uniform grids. The discrete LANS-alpha and LES models are solved using an asynchronous multi-core parallel solver. The simulations are performed for a range of CFL numbers to obtain the most turbulent solution for each CFL number. Highly turbulent solutions are projected to reduced order using a gradient projection method. The results are compared with a high resolution simulation and good agreement is observed for flow statistics.

The generation interval (GI) is the time between the infectious period of an individual and when they would become contagious again. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the GI was found to be decreasing in many countries, indicating that the virus could remain viable in the population for a shorter time. This could help the virus spread throughout the population more quickly, or it could lead to increased uncertainty about when an individual is contagious, which could compromise vaccination strategies or other mitigation strategies that depend on knowing the timing of infection. To understand this phenomenon, we collected data on COVID-19 cases in Australia, Brazil, Italy, and the United States. We find that changes in GI vary over time, following trends in cumulative cases. This allowed us to build a model of GI that reproduces the observed time series with high accuracy. We also find that changes in GI are strongly correlated with changes in cumulative cases, both globally and on annual timescales, which suggests that the observed contraction in GI is a global phenomenon. Our findings indicate that real-time monitoring of COVID-19 GI can help public health authorities better understand the COVID-19 pandemic and respond more effectively.

We present a spectral analysis method, VESPA, which makes use of automated algorithms to extract the history of star formation and the metallicity of galaxies from the spectra of intermediate-widthband filters. We use our code to extract the star formation rate (SFR) and median metallicity from spectra of Lick index space in four redshift bins between 0.1z = 0.07 - 0.2. We find that at all epochs the median metallicity is super-solar and at low redshift the median star formation is below 1% of the volume-averaged value. Our derived SFR history is in good agreement with those from the Lyman-alphaemitter population selected from the same data. We show that our method is able to reliably recover these metrics with measurement uncertainties below 10% at all redshifts and typically 5% at high redshift. Finally, we show that at high redshift the SFR from VESPA is in good agreement with that from the Lyman-alphaemitter population selected with less IGM filters and further indicates that reionization was near-complete by z > 6.

A CCD BV (Bayer to Visual) survey has been made of 42 open clusters, covering a range ofclusters from the Upper mglimFs down to the Lower Chromospherics branch. This work has been done in collaboration with Dr I. Sterzik of Geneva. The data have been taken from the EDD pro gram at the ESO-MPI 2.2m telescope, La Silla, Chile, and have been reduced atObservatoire de Haute-Provence (OHP), France. Wherever possible, comparisons have been made with existing, independently calculated, and independently calculated estimates of these star clusters' basic parameters, most previously published by Duflot et al. (SNF, Switzerland). Excellent agreement has been found in all but four cases, for which it is suspected that the older estimates were incorrect. The comparisons--which generally consider an rms difference of less than 2% acceptable--indicate that for the majority of the clusters' parameters an error of better than 5% can be expected. Mean representativity errors of better than 10% are found for 35 of the 42 clusters. In 9 clusters a lower level ofaccuracy (20-30%) is to be expected. Excellent agreement between the independently calculated reddening values is found.The resulting data set is the most extensive homogeneous catalogue of the fundamental parameters of 42 star clusters accessible from the internet. The 42 clusters' basic parameters (iron cluster mass, rms, and reddening values) have been determined to an acceptable accuracy of less than 5% for most parameters, with a mean representativity error of better than 10%. The accuracy of the reddening values is excellent.

We present the method and the related code PASTEL to determine the age and metallicity of stellar populations from their color. This is achieved by comparing the observed colors to those of synthetic populations built with the v2.3.2 Geneva evolutionary tracks with massive Asa Z Phoenix NextGenJK99SiWD. Comparison to empirical colour-colour diagrams yields the best age-metallicity pair for a given object. We present the results for a sample of 324 local galaxies and illustrate our ability to break the age-metallicity degeneracy by applying this technique to archival ACS and WFC3 observations of the Fornax and Centaurus clusters. We find that the age of the stellar populations varies between 10 and 13 Gyr, with a median value of +0.5 Gyr, and that the metallicities are between 8 and 10 dex, with a median value of +0.5 dex solar metallicity, with a median value of +0.7 dex.

We further our study of closed string field theory around the stable solution of quintic Calabi-Yau hypersurface. By analyzing the one-loop moduli space approximation, we first present the generic structure of the theory, and their corresponding marginal deformations, and propose the first-order effective action. Next, we apply our results to study the discrete states in thetheory. We first present the explicit form of wave-functions on the basis of recent works. Then, we show that there exists a hidden symmetry in the theory, and derive the corresponding constraints on the interaction vertices. Together with the one-loop result, our result provides a complete description of the discrete states at quartic order. This work was done in collaboration with Hitoshi Nishino and Shota Komatsu. Closed bosonic string field theory around the stable solution of quintic Calabi-Yau is studied at cubic and quartic order in this work. Generically, the theory contains marginal deformations and their corresponding marginal deformations, and propose the first-order effective action. By studying the discrete states, we first present the explicit form of wave-functions on the basis of recent works. Then, we show that there exists a hidden symmetry in the theory, and derive the corresponding constraints on the interaction vertices. In particular, we show that there exist discrete states at cubic order and at quartic order respectively.

The $p$-adic Haar multiresolution analysis (MRA) is a general framework for constructing non-equivalent wavelet systems. It is natural to ask if there is any suitable system for all the $p$-adic MRA. In this paper, we construct a $p$-adic MRA using pseudo-differential operators (PDOs), a general framework for defining wavelets on non-smooth spaces. By generalizing the PDO definition for the $p$-adic MRA, we show that the sequence of difference operators, induced by PDOs, constitutes an optimal $p$-adic MRA, in the sense that it is non-redundant, complete in the sense of the kernels and Parseval. As an application, we construct wavelets with Strang-type stability and we show that a certain PDO is a sequence of difference operators. The $p$-Adic Haar MRA is a fundamental tool in the study of wavelet theory. It was introduced by Christ and Journé in the seminal paper "DecrConstruction of Wavelets byydr Similar to the Haar Basis" in *SIAM J. Mathemat. Anal.*, Vol. 17, no. 3, pp. 310–348 (1986). Although $p$-adic numbers are usually thought of as a bizarre substitute for the real numbers, they have many advantages over the usual real numbers. For example, they satisfy the completeness and the distributive laws. These two properties allow one to use the tools from real analysis, such as the Cauchy sequences and the limit operations, to study the $p$-adic numbers in a very effective way. As a result, one can prove the fundamental theorems about the $p$-adic numbers, such as the completeness theorem and the density theorem. Based on the $p$-adic MRA, Christ and Journé developed the theory of compactly supported wavelets in *Fourier Analysis and Constr. Func. Appl.*, Ed. by H. G. Funcke, R. A. Marks II, Lect. Notes Math., 1209, pp. 127–165 (1986). In recent years, a growing number of people have used the $p$-adic MRA in various fields such as time series analysis, non-Archimedean probability, mathematical physics and number theory. It is very interesting to find applications of the $p$-adic MRA in these fields. The fact that the $p$-adic MRA has many similarities with the classical MRA on the one hand and many nice properties on the other hand make it a good candidate for many applications. It is one of the motivations of this paper to study the applications of $p$-adic MRA in these fields. Simulations of the IGM show that cooling processes play a vital role in determining the large-scale structure of the universe. These simulations require assumptions about cooling processes active at small scales, which can mimic the observed large-scale structure if these processes leave their signatures on large scales. One such process is cooling, which may occur naturally in the plasma. Molecular hydrogen and metals may also cool the plasma, although the importance of these processes in the IGM is unclear because these processes have not been self-consistently implemented in the model. Here we present a method to capture these cooling processes in simulations, and apply it to a model in which galaxies generate hot gas and inject metals into the IGM. We find that including these processes can decrease the amplitude of linear fluctuations by 8% and decrease the small-scale power at wavenumbers 1≤k[Mpc-1]<3. We argue that these fluctuations could in turn increase the small-scale density of dark matter halos, leading to more galaxies in the redshift. Our results suggest that metal and molecule cooling have a significant impact on the large-scale structure of the universe, but improved treatments of these processes are required to determine their impact on the matter distribution in more detail.

In proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of \sqrt{s}=14TeV, events with a photon and at least one jet have been selected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC. In the fiducial region corresponding to one direct photon and at least four jets, the observed (expected) cross section is in agreement with the next-to-leading order (NLO) QCD prediction (ME+PS). A fiducial photon jet tagger is presented. It yields an estimate of the direct photon fraction in the photon+jet sample with an uncertainty comparable to the next-to-leading order QCD calculation. The measured jetshape variables are used to compare the results obtained with deep neural networks against a leading order QCD Monte Carlo event generator. The artificial neural networks achieve a better performance than the leading order generator at the QCD NLO level. Directed percolation (DP) is a new approach for spreader-stifler dynamics, in which a state of active sites gives way to a state of passive sites with probability p, or to an active state with probability (1-p). In this work, we study steady-state properties of DP on finite one-dimensional lattices using extensive numerical simulations and a recently proposed approach based on finite-size scaling (FSS). This approach combines numerical simulations for system sizes up to L=1023 with analytical predictions for the giant component size and scaling of the number of components, also for system sizes of up to L=1023. Our results suggest that on one-dimensional lattices, DP exhibits a continuous phase transition at p_c=0.5 between a phase with a single giant component, which contains a nonzero absorbing fraction for p>p_c, and a phase with no giant component. The FSS approach appears to be very useful for studying models with absorbing states, since it does not require equilibration, and thus it can be applied to much larger system sizes than traditional simulation s.

Theory of Two-Photon Interactions with Broadband Down-Converted Light and Entangled Photons entangled photon pairs produced by spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) are widely used for demonstrations of quantum non-locality and quantum entanglement. SPDC, which is also known as frequency down-conversion, occurs when a single mode of the electromagnetic field is excited in a nonlinear crystal to produce photons of different frequencies. Two photons produced by SPDC have some unique properties, such as correlated amplitudes and phases and anticorrelation of their frequencies. These properties can be useful for quantum information processing and communication. However, two-photon interference based on these properties is difficult to perform. In this paper, we propose a theory for two-photon interference based on broadband down-converted light and entangled photons produced by SPDC. We use a general model that can be used to describe two-photon interference with broadband down-converted light and entangled photons. This model can be used to simulate and optimize the setup for two-photon interference with broadband down-converted light and entangled photons. We derive a phase-matching condition, which limits the frequency range for SPDC. We also introduce broadband down-converted light generated by quasi-phase-matching and describe the down-conversion processes to the bandwidth limit. We present the theory with detailed calculations.

. Surface nematic liquid crystals are partially ordered phases with rod-like molecules aligned along a particular axis. In the bulk, the alignment direction is usually constant for all positions, but at the surface the molecules may be freely orientated. This leads to an enrichment of nematic order at the surfaces, which is sometimes referred to as surface nematic order. Here we present a simple Landau-de Gennes method for the description of a surface nematic liquid crystal, focussing on the case where the surface enrichment is weak. In our approach, the director is described by a continuous variable θ(z, x), where z is the normal direction to the surface and x is the lateral spatial variable. The order parameter adopts a constant value s in the surface layer, leading to a surface free energy functional which can be minimized with respect to s and θ. By applying different spatial approximations we are able to characterize the isotropic, N- and Sm-Nematic phases and the corresponding phase transitions. To quantify the degree of order, we introduce pair correlation functions g12(x) and g22(x), which make a Nematic phase take on a non-zero constant value. The values of g12 and g22 depend on the spatial correlation of the order parameter, and can be determined by solving an approximate anisotropic Laplace equation. From the functional we are able to derive a Cahn-Hilliard equation for the order parameter evolution, which can be simplified to a linear non-local diffusion equation by performing a gradient expansion. This diffusion equation can be solved using an appropriate random initial condition to give the order parameter distribution at long times, and from this we are able to extract the values of g12 and g22 at long distances. As an application, we discuss the case of a surface enrichment which varies quadratically with z, and which leads to modified power-law decay of g12 and g22. Finally, we also present the corresponding results for the special case of a step function surface enrichment.

On 2022 October 05, the isolated neutron star RBS 1774 became X-ray brighter for the first time in approximately 20 years as it went into outburst. Subsequent X-ray and multiwavelength observations detected the source to be localized to a 17 square arcsecond region , based on Right Ascension 17 h 35 min, Declination -35 d , 00" (equinox J2000). This improves upon previous localizedizations by an order of magnitude in both precision and accuracy. Subsequent observations revealed that RBS 1774 is most likely an MSP binary in a highly elliptical orbit with a period of 19.1 hours, with a white dwarf passing within approximately 12 R_NS (where R_NS is the radius of the neutron star) every 3.2 days. This is the first observed system of an isolated neutron star with a white dwarf companion. Analysis of the pulsations from RBS 1774 revealed a rotation period of approximately 13.8 milliseconds, the fastest period of any neutron star. Additionally, observations with the NuSTAR and XMM-Newton satellites have determined that the orbit is nearly circular, and that the system most likely has an inclination of ~45°. This measurement of the spin and orbital parameters gives new information on the equation of state of neutron star matter.

Memory and glassiness are ubiquitous in both natural and artificial systems. It is well-known that the metastable state of a supercooled liquid becomes unstable at a critical temperature of freezing, leading to the formation of a glassy state. Similarly, the failure of a digital circuit becomes inevitable when the operating temperature reaches a certain point, owing to the presence of noise. In this Letter, we investigate the ageing memory in a driven vortex system. By employing the time-resolved scanning laser Doppler vibrometry, we experimentally demonstrate that the metastable state of an infinite longitudinal wave becomes unstable with the propagation of wave number at a critical value, leading to the formation of a glassy state. We also clarify that the ageing memory is related to the failure of an information processing in the wave system, i.e., memory and glassiness are two sides of the same coin. Our findings not only enrich the understandings of the glass transition in wave systems, but also have potential applications in information processing with memory.

We present the results of a search for tidal dwarf galaxies candidates in a sample of ultraluminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs). Using data from the Sloan e Sky Survey DR13 and UKIRT Infrared Deep Space Survey UDS fields, we identify 77 pairs of ULIRG s with projected physical separations between 3 and 30 kpc and classified them visually into five categories:interacting/merging, distorted, linear, random and strong bar. We compare the number and colors of the potential TDG candidates in each pair as a function of their separation and stellar mass of the host galaxy. We conclude that the number and types of potential TDG candidates strongly depend on the host galaxy stellar mass, with a total of 40% of the mergers showing only very weak tidal features. In addition, we estimate the total number of potential TDGs produced in these ULIRG s as R<unk>6 and we estimate a minimum of 15 TDG stellar masses ranging from 10^6 to 10^9 M⊙. This number and the derived minimum TDG mass scale s back to the ULIRG separation as R−6. Our findings suggest that the majority of the ULIRG systems will be able to form TDGs during their interaction but only a small number of them will evolve into fully fledged TDGs with stellar masses larger than 10^9 M⊙.

We present an atlas of circumnuclear regions of 75 nearby Seyfert galaxies observed with the Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) aboard the Hubble Space Telescope (HST). These galaxies, which span a range in Hubble type, are among the most extensively observed Seyferts with HST. Using an unified model of active galactic nucleus (AGN) structure in which the central engine is surrounded by an accretion region, Broad Line Region, and torus, we investigate the properties of the circumnuclear regions in these galaxies. We find evidence for spatially resolved warm absorption in the near-UV in 57% of the sample. The warm absorbers are characterized by a multi-phase structure with Doppler parameters ranging from ∼30 to ∼250 km s-1, turbulent velocities from ~10 to <unk>1000 km s-1, and covering factors from a few percent to nearly 100%. The amount of soft X-ray flux absorbed by the warm absorber is strongly correlated with the amount of high-ionization [O VI] absorption, suggesting that the same gas is responsible for both absorptions. The multi-phase nature of the absorbing gas implies that it is composed of numerous clouds with small, non-uniform covering factors. We estimate the total column densities of individual species from the model fits and find that O VI, N V, and C IV are often the dominant ions, while gas-phase oxygen may be depleted with respect to solar abundances. We also find evidence for dust in the form of narrow absorption lines in 56% of the sample. We compare our results to recent models of dusty AGN winds, finding that the observed properties of the warm absorbers can be compared using obscuring columns of a few times 1022 km s-1 and velocities of a few thousand km s-1. Our atlas provides the best currently available view of the circumnuclear regions of AGN and the first such atlas of its kind in the near-UV. This atlas demonstrates the feasibility of using the HST ACS to study circumnuclear regions of Seyfert galaxies in the near-UV. We find that the properties of the absorbing gas phase are generally similar to those of the models of dusty AGN winds.

We find evidence for the existence of an extreme type-II superconductor with strong pairing, as the temperature dependence of the muon spin rotation signal indicates the presence of lines of nodes in the energy gap. This observation is further supported by field-dependent measurements of the magnetic field size of the superconducting signal. We finally evidence clear and sharp transitions from superconducting phase to normal state, consistent with the conventional properties of a type-II superconductor, as confirmed by the field-dependence of the normal state muon depolarization rate. The combination of extremely high-transition temperature, super-strong coupling and field-tuned superconductor phase, makes the MgB2 thin-walled cylinder a very promising new candidate for the applications of high-field superconducting magnets and sensors.

At the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), Standard Model (SM) expectations are usually validated by measuring its corresponding effects in diverse final states. In this paper, the results of the total and differential cross sections as well as the forward-backward asymmetry for the top pair production process at $\sqrt{s}=1.96$ TeV are presented. Furthermore, the limits at 95% confidence level on anomalous ZZgamma and Zgammagamma couplings are obtained by comparing the measured observables with the corresponding predictions of a general two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) with CP invariance. The experiments are performed using proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=1.96$ TeV recorded by the CMS experiment at the LHC. The total and differential cross sections of the top pair production process are measured as a function of the top pair invariant mass, $M(t\bar{t})$, for different top quark polarization states. In addition, the forward-backward asymmetry is determined as a function of $M(t\bar{t})$ for two different helicity configurations of the top quark. Furthermore, the helicity angles of the top quark are used to discriminate between the SM predictions and a model with anomalous ZZgamma couplings. Anomalous ZZgamma and Zgammagamma couplings could originate from extended Higgs sectors such as two-Higgs-doublet models (2HDMs). In this model, a complex Yukawa coupling between the top quark and the proton field can induce four types of anomalous couplings. For each type, both sign alternatives are investigated: charge-odd and charge-even. The obtained results are in good agreement with the SM predictions and no significant deviations are found. Assuming the 2HDM with CP invariance, the limits at 95% confidence level on anomalous ZZgamma and Zgammagamma couplings are derived. No evidence of anomalous ZZgamma or Zgammagamma couplings is found. Limits are set on the combinations of the couplings of both signs. For the first time, lower limits of $0.68$, $0.60$, $0.50$ and $0.45$ are established at the 68% confidence level for combinations of the parameters corresponding to the types i, ii, iii, and iv, respectively.

A new parameterization of the cosine of the Michel in channel ξ, in terms of the neutrino type, ν, and the effective electron neutrino mass, θ, has been developed. The new parameterization, ξ = ξ(ν, θ), is valid for any ν and satisfies ξ(ν = λ, θ) = ξ(ν, θ = 0) for all θ. Previously, ξ was parameterized in terms of the neutrino type and the effective electron neutrino mass, θ_{ν_{e}} ≡ ξ(ν = ν_{e}, θ = 0)$, where ν_{e} is the electron neutrino eigenstate. In the νν -catalyzed (ν->ν) channel, this parameterization corresponds to the traditional (3+1) description of ξ via three parameters, the neutrino mixing angle, θ_{13}, the CP phase, Δ, and the effective electron neutrino mass, θ_{ν_e}. We present a new parameterization of ξ in terms of the neutrino type and the effective muon neutrinos mass, θ_{\mu\nu} ≡ <unk> (<unk> = μ, θ = 0), where μ is the muon neutrino eigenstate. This new parameterization allows for a model-independent comparison between the ξ results obtained with the (3+1) and (3+2) descriptions of ξ. The new ξ parameterization reduces the number of free parameters in ξ phenomenological models from three to two. It also simplifies the comparison between ξ results obtained using the (3+1) and (3+2) parameterizations by eliminating the effective electron neutrino mass. We make this simplification explicit in a modified version of the Giunti φ-theorem proof to show that the effective muon neutrino mass and a CP-violating phase are sufficient to characterize the propagation of neutrinos across flavor space. Finally, we demonstrate the application of the new parameterization by comparing it to results obtained using the traditional (3+1) description.

Semi-structured text, e.g. , documents from the web or engineering documents, are composed of implicit schemas, i.e. possible relationships between the concept words, and explicit tuples of co-occurrence between the concept words. In this paper, we present a dynamic user-defined similarity searching (DUSDSS) model that incorporates both implicit and explicit relationships for semi-structured text retrieval. Based on the user-defined semantic space, we design a similarity function to measure the semantic similarity between search terms and retrieve the relevant documents ranked by these similarities. In order to accurately understand the semantics of users’ interest and expand the coverage of document collection, we further propose to generate document semantic representations from multiple perspectives, such as topic, author and document topic networks. To efficiently compute the relevance between user queries and documents, we present a continuous space search strategy, which applies negative sampling to approximate the semantic similarity ranking metric. Finally, we conduct experiments on two public datasets and the results show that our model can outperform state-of-the-art methods on both explicit and implicit semantic similarity evaluations.

Binary microlensing light curves can probe denser regions of the lensing galaxy, determine separatetimes of events in the images, and break the degeneracy of the massfunction of binary systems. These benefits, coupled with the relatively ease of detection with existing survey methods, make binary microlensing a promising tool for cosmology. With the increasing number of events detected by microlensing surveys, it is now possible to test for deviations from strict caustic crossing behavior. In this work, we analyze a large sample of binary-light curves from OGLE-2015-BLG-0341, show that deviations from caustic crossing behavior can be explained by a finite source effect, and present an empirical model to predict lightcurve shape in the absence of causticcrossing features. With this empirical model, we accurately predict lightcurve shape for 21 additional binary- microlensing systems, and we show that these can also be explained by a finite source effect. We compare our results to theoretical models, finding that one-dimensional dynamical models for the lensing galaxy produce lightcurves that are qualitatively different from the empirical model we present here. Our findings demonstrate that binary microlensing can provide additional measurements of the lensing system that can be used to distinguish between theoretical models of the lensing galaxy, which will help break the degeneracy in cosmology analyses using microlensing."

A study of the incidence of C IV absorbers along the sightlines to z ≥ 0.47 gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) indicates a high degree of clustering of C IV systems near the line of sight. Six of eleven gamma-ray bursts have more than one C IV system within 60,000 km s-1 of the line of sight. The nearest two C IV systems are separated by 45,000 km s-1 on average and no burst is more than 5,000 km s-1 without multiple C IV systems within 60,000 km s-1 of the line of sight. The most likely explanation for the high incidence of C IV absorption along these lines of sight is that a population of dark collapsed structures is passing along our line of sight. We estimate the total matter in these dark collapsed structures is on the order of 1022 -1023 solar masses. The dimensions of these structures are approximately 10-4 to 10-5 parsecs, which is approximately one ten-thousandth to one one-thousandth the distance between the Earth and the Sun. The clustering and relative proximity of the C IV systems indicates that these dark collapsed structures likely are located at typical distances of 10 parsecs from the sites of gamma-ray bursts. Furthermore, the inferred dimensions of these structures are consistent with the size distribution of black holes that may form from the collapse of dark primordial structures such as carbon clusters, large moons, or galaxies. If confirmed, this discovery has profound implications for modeling the demographics of black holes, their interactions with their environments, and the reprocessing of electromagnetic radiation in their broad-line regions.

A charged sphere can focus high-energy charged particles. This is due to the electrostatic repulsion between the particles and the sphere. The equation of the motion of an electric particle is hard to solve. However, one can obtain an effective momentum approximation, which can describe the particle trajectory well. The effective momentum is a function of the radius of the sphere, the initial velocity of the particle, and the charge and the mass of the particle. The effective momentum approximation is good for two situations. The first is for a very large initial velocity of the particle, which spreads over several times the electrostatic potential of the sphere. The second is for the particle radius smaller than the radius of the sphere. For example, Titania, the subject of a scientific paper, is a homogeneously charged sphere and can focus particles of a diameter of less than ten nanometers. The electrostatic potential of Titania is approximately equal to one volt. For such a small particle, the initial velocity needed to be focused by Titania is approximately equal to one million meters per second. Even for such a large initial velocity, the effective momentum approximation is valid because the particle radius is less than one nanometer, which is ten thousand times smaller than the radius of Titania (one hundred nanometers). The effective momentum approximation is validated by the fact that Titania can focus a particle of diameter less than ten nanometers, while the force of electrostatic repulsion between the proton and Titania is approximately thirty billion times larger than the weight of the proton (one thousand trillion tons versus one billion kilograms). The effective momentum approximation describes the particle trajectory as a function of the radius of the sphere, the charge and the mass of the particle, and the initial velocity of the particle. Solving the equation, we get that the radius of Titania is approximately equal to one hundred nanometers. The Leo II dwarf spheroidal galaxy is one of the most ancient objects in the Universe. Recent Hubble Space Telescope imaging with the F336W and F438W telescopes has allowed us to determine the metallicity and color of a large sample of Leo II dwarf spheroidal stars, which, in combination with ground-based high-precision kinematics, allowed us to construct a detailed chemical and photometric full phase-space stellar density distribution. We find that the total luminosity-velocity velocity dispersion decreases with increasing distance from the center of Leo II, which is most likely the result of the net loss of mass to unobservable stars at a greater distance, or some form of dark matter. We also detect a significant dispersion in the line-of-sight velocities of our stars, and compute the mass of Leo II within 100 kpc to be (2.2\pm0.4) x 10^8 M_\odot. Finally, we compare the total luminosity-velocity dispersion and mass-to-light ratios of Leo II with those of the Milky Way, Andromeda, and other local dwarf spheroidals and find Leo II to be a most promising target for the next generation of wide field imageries from the Large Synoptic Survey Telescope.

In this work we study the impact of $(1+z)^6$ terms on the cosmological parameters estimated from the growth rate of linear structures. These terms were recently found in the Lagrangian expansion of the universe (Alimohammadi et al. 2011, Padilla & Baskaran 2012). These terms are significant at high redshifts and play a more significant role in the clustering amplitude of matter distributions. This paper tests these higher order terms on their ability to better constrain cosmological parameters using a Fisher matrix analysis. We find that when the $(1+z)^6$ terms are included, uncertainties in $\Omega_m$ and $\sigma_8$ decrease by 7% and 12%, respectively. When combined with Planck and the same priors these errors decrease by 10% and 14%, respectively. When combined with the WiggleZ Dark Energy Survey and the same priors these errors decrease by 16% and 20%, respectively. We also use these terms to fit cosmological parameters and find that $\Omega_m$ and $\sigma_8$ are underestimated by 1.5% and 5% if these terms are not included. These results show that the clustering amplitude of matter distributions is more sensitive to the behavior of the universe at high redshifts and that these higher order terms must be taken into account when fitting cosmological models to the growth rate of structures.

This article studies peculiar features in the distribution of the Ursa Major supercluster of galaxies. Peculiar motions are among the biggest problems in modern cosmology. They are observed in the distribution of galaxies. Standard $\Lambda$CDM model of the universe predicts that galaxies moved from their places. But in the region of the Ursa Major supercluster all galaxies have peculiar motions close to zero. The article presents an analysis of the Supercluster Catalog, which was created using spectroscopic data from the SDSS and other projects. The Catalog contains the data about the coordinates, distances and radial velocity of 15000 galaxies in the region of the Ursa Major supercluster. It was shown that the distribution of distances between galaxies has two maxima corresponding to the distance between the Local Group and the Ursa Major cluster and the distance between the Local Supercluster and the Ursa Major cluster. In the Local Supercluster the radial velocity has a maximum at the border of the Local Supercluster and goes to zero at the border of the Ursa Major cluster. The described features are explained using a hypothesis of the still existing gravitational attraction between the clusters.

Monte Carlo (MC) simulations have been performed to investigate the dynamic response of a silver (Ag) monolayer adsorbed on Au(100) to an oscillatory variation of the chemical potential. Upon an increase of the chemical potential, the Ag atoms adsorb at sites with higher chemical potentials, leading to a compactification of the layer. Upon a decrease of the chemical potential, the Ag atoms desorb, leading to an expansion of the layer. We show that the dynamic behavior of the Ag monolayer is strongly dependent on the heating and cooling rates. In particular, at slow heating and cooling rates, a sizable hysteresis is observed. The dynamic behavior is analyzed in the framework of the generalized Lindemann model, which accounts for changes in the chemical potential of the adsorbed atoms upon heating and cooling. It is known that small changes in the chemical potential of components of a complex system may cause large excursions of the correspondingGibbs free energy. Depending on the heating and cooling rates, these excursions may induce dynamic phenomena such as hysteresis. Here, we report the for the first time observation of hysteresis in the dynamic behavior of a Ag monolayer upon an oscillatory variation of the chemical potential. Our findings have important implications for the modeling and interpretation of experimental data, and for the control of surface diffusion in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and molecular microbial epitaxy (MBE) growth processes.

Strong lensing, also called gravitational lensing, is the phenomenon by which light from a distant star or galaxy is bent due to the Gravitational field of cluster galaxies. It is one of the most powerful methods to study the dark matter distribution in clusters of galaxies. Bayesian inference provides a robust framework to extract the maximum information from the raw imaging data, while appropriately handling missing or erroneous data points. I present a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm to model the cluster mass distribution, combining strong and weak lensing data. I demonstrate the performance of the algorithm on both simulated and real data using a variety of tools to diagnose the weak and strong lensing properties of the MCMC chains. The method presented in this paper can be extended to study other astrophysical problems which can be modeled with MCMC methods. This paper presents the kinematic design of a 3-dof hybrid manipulator which includes both a dual-quaternion-based rotation kinematics and a novel 3-DOF snake-like structure for end-effector motion. The proposed structure integrates the advantages of the dual quaternion and 3-DOF snake-like manipulators, and it is more concise and easier to integrate with complex control algorithms. The proposed hybrid manipulator can achieve large flexibility and dexterity by combining the 3-DOF snake-like structure with a dual quaternion-based rotation kinematics. In this paper, the hybrid configuration is firstly constructed using a dual quaternion-based rotation kinematics, which provides a flexible and compact representation. Then, a novel 3-DOF snake-like structure, which provides a large motion amplitude, is introduced to balance the flexibility and dexterity for the hybrid manipulator. To facilitate the kinematics analysis and synthesis, the singularities of the proposed hybrid manipulator are analyzed and a series of singular transformations are developed. Two numerical examples are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid manipulator.

Soccer results often depend on the type of the team or the individual player. Goal scoring patterns can be skewed by a team's or player's current performance or overall offensive scheme. In this paper we explore an additional variable correlated to individual/team performance: motivation. We propose the self-affirmation model which states that a player/team will tend to adopt a strategy which they find attractive. We provide empirical evidence to support this statement by analysing archived goals from football competitions. We find that the distribution of goals by the average attractive goal scoring strategy is a good fit to the observed goal distributions. The implications of this work are wide-ranging, for example, it has applications for predicting outcomes of football matches as well as players/teams underlying strategy. The self-affirmation model has two facets. One facet is that a person or a team will tend to adopt a strategy which they find attractive. This has implications for many sports, from predicting the outcomes of football matches to understanding individual player development. Another aspect of the self-affirmation model is that human behaviour is complex. We can simplify human motivation with a few general tendencies. We have evidence to support the applicability of these general tendencies to football goals scored. These two facets of the self-affirmation model are developed and empirically tested. We find that the average attractive goal scoring strategy is a good fit to the goal scoring patterns in football competitions. Additionally we find that a person or a team will tend to adopt a strategy which they find attractive. Implications for predicting outcomes of football matches are outlined. The generalizability of the findings is discussed, and practical examples of the implications are given. This paper provides evidence to support a wideranging model of human behaviour: the self-affirmation model. By examining human motivations we can predict the outcome of sporting competitions. For example, the total goal tally of a football team can be predicted based on the average attractive goal scoring strategy, along with the individual goal tallies of the players. There are several implications for applying this model to player/team development and competitive sports. We can predict an individual player's performance by considering their motivation, and personalising training programs accordingly. Coaching strategies can be designed to influence team performance based on the motivation of the team. Self-assembled quantum dots (SAQDs) provide a synthetic route to precisely engineer semiconductor nanostructures with tailored material properties. As such, SAQDs hold promise for developing next-generation optical technologies including light-emitting diodes (LEDs), lasers, and bioimaging sensors. Previous studies have demonstrated that the crystal quality of SAQDs strongly influences their optoelectronic properties; however, it is notoriously difficult to precisely control SAQD crystal quality during synthesis. Here, we report epitaxial growth of SAQDs, wherein the crystal quality of the SAQD is contingent upon the crystal quality of the substrate on which it is grown. Using linearly polarized InAs/GaAs self-assembled quantum dots, we characterize their photoluminescence (PL) polarized with respect to the [112] and [001] GaAs crystal directions. We find that the SAQD's PL is linearly polarized with respect to the substrate's [112] direction for all crystal orientations, while it is not linearly polarized with respect to the [001] direction for any crystal orientation. This result suggests that, in addition to the previously observed bulk dipoles in SAQDs, the crystal quality of SAQDs is also dictated by the epitaxial relationship between the dot and substrate. By focusing on the crystal quality of the substrate and dot, this work establishes a pathway for precisely controlling SAQD optical properties and demonstrates the feasibility of this approach for developing next-generation optoelectronic technologies.

Runtime verification uses additional information about the timing of events to prove that a system is running correctly. Most existing runtime verification tools either require the designer to provide timing annotations or perform partial verification by demonstrating that a property holds for all possible timing exceptions. In this paper we describe an approach to verify system -level timing relations without requiring the designer to provide timing annotations. We use a separation logic to statically prove the absence of certain timing relations, and we use model checking to prove the presence of other timing relations. We use monadic difference logic to characterize the allowable timing exceptions. We evaluate our method on real-world synthetically-timed benchmarks and demonstrate that we are able to verify correct timing relations in many cases, and we are able to prove incorrect timing relations in other cases. This work was partially funded by the Australian Research Council (Discovery Grants DP170100655 and DP180100709).

This significantly reduces the number of operations needed to simulate a spin system, while achieving second order accuracy in the time step. A the recent years, the diquarks, as effective degrees of freedom of strong interaction, have been widely investigated in various areas of physics, such as nuclear physics, particle physics and condensed matter physics. In this work, we investigate the diquarks within the framework of color-flavor locked (CFL) quark matter, which is the only possible stable phase of dense quark matter. By considering both the scalar and vector diquarks, we calculate the corresponding mass spectrum of mesons, and observe that, in the CFL phase, the diquarks form both scalar and vector channels, with the isospin I=0 and 1, spin 0 and 1, and flavor n and p modes mixed, respectively. We find that, compared with the nucleon mass, the diquark masses are relatively smaller in the CFL phase. Furthermore, we calculate the mass spectrum of mesons in the CFL phase, and observe that, besides the usual scalar and axial-vector mesons, some exotic mesons, such as the isovector scalar meson and isovector scalar diquark, axial-vector diquark and isovector vector meson, could be possibly formed. The mass spectrum of the diquarks and mesons in the CFL quark matter might provide useful information for the structure of compact stars, and might be useful for determining the structure of compact stars in future .

Mo is a relatively light transition element and an important electropositive element in the Earth's crust. Its nearly constant mixing ratio with molybdenum disulfite (MoS 2 ) in the ocean surface serves as an important mechanism of crustal modification. Mo has a hexagonal close packed structure with anbody expansion coefficient of approximately 11.6 × 10-6 K−1, making it vulnerable to many important geological processes such as metamorphism and igneous processes. Molybdenum sulfide is a common product of these processes and exhibits a simple cubic structure with anbody expansion coefficient of 14.2 × 10-6 K−1. However, experimental results have shown that shock transition temperatures in molybdenum sulfide are significantly lower than those predicted by the earlier obtained cubic-to-hexagonal structural phase transition temperature. To better understand the shock behavior of molybdenum and the discrepancy between the cubic and hexagonal phase transition temperatures, we performed an efficient series of high-pressure experiments with shock-transmission retarders made of synthetic molybdenum disulfide using the high-pressure shock-transmission apparatus. We established shock-transmission curves for the molybdenum sulfide at pressures between 0.3 and 5 GPa, and we determined the maximum shock transition temperatures of approximately 1630 K at 0.3 GPa and approximately 1530 K at 5 GPa. By analyzing these results and comparing them to the Shock and Impact Effects Database, we conclude that shock velocities above 4.8 km/s cause the cubic structure to transform into a hexagonal structure. The structural phase transition temperature of 29.7 ± 1.1 K<unk>1 determined from our experiments is significantly lower than the value of 39 GPa determined using earlier experiments, which used less efficient shock transmission methods.

In this work, we study analog neural networks with temporally fluctuating synaptic weights, i.e. a noisy neural network. Such noise may model the effect of random mutations in molecules and can significantly improve the performance of the network. We employ the Thouless-Anderson-Palmer (TAP) approach to derive the phase diagram of such a noisy neural network. Depending on the number of weight and input noise realizations, the system is in the synchronized state, where all neurons share the same output, or in the desynchronized state. In the latter case, the outputs of individual neurons are independent. We also consider the case of a noisy analog neural network in which the individual weight and input noise are zero, which corresponds to a purely analog neural network. We find that even in this case, the reduction of weight noise improves the ability of the network to discriminate between different patterns. In particular, it facilitates the separation of closely related patterns and prevents overfitting.

Charge ordering (CO) in half-doped manganites is an important issue in the field of solid state physics. Although there have been numerous investigations on the origins of CO in manganites, it remains a mystery. Here we present a combined experimental and theoretical study of CO in the layered perovskite-like manganites, (La_{0.5}Ca_{0.5})MnO_{3}±x, with x = 0.4 and 0.5. We find that the magnetic, structural, transport, and NMR properties are quite similar for these two manganites, which allowed for a clear separation of the effects of charge and spin degrees of freedom. While the former induces stripe-type CO, the latter leads to weak charge disproportion (WCD) and drives the stripe fluctuations. These results indicate that the leading mechanisms for CO in layered perovskite-like manganites are WCD and stripe fluctuations. The occurrence of WCD has important implications for the correlation between charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom, which should be carefully considered in exploring the origins of CO in manganites.

Extrasolar planets, unlike the Solar System planets, have no moon to stabilize their temperatures. As a result, hot Jupiters, which have orbits closer to their host stars than the Earth is to the Sun, can have surface temperatures that vary by 1000K or more as they rotate about their host stars. The dips in surface temperature are synchronized with the planet's rotation, and the duration of these dips is dependent on the planet's atmospheric composition and, more specifically, the opacity of the atmosphere to visible and infrared radiation. Hot Jupiters with thicker, less transparent atmospheres have deeper dips. Conversely, planets with thinner atmospheres and/or more efficient circulation patterns, such as tidally locked planets with dayside/nightside temperatures equal, tend to have more shallow dips. Thus, the time period that a hot Jupiter may be considered "hot" (with surface temperatures above 750K) is inversely related to the duration of the "night" on such a planet. Using the Wide Angle Space Explorer (WISE) satellite, I analyzed nearly 3000 transits of 1776 hot Jupiters and found that many of these planets have significant phase variations in their infrared fluxes. I characterized the correlation between the observed phase variations and other planet and star parameters, using a multivariate linear regression model. This model could be used to determine the day-night termperature contrast of an unknown planet from the WISE data alone. I also simulated the observed phase variations from the WISE data for different climate scenarios, in order to better understand how various planet properties affect the resulting temperature variations. I found that a hot Jupiter's atmospheric composition and heat transport efficiency play the biggest role in determining the observed dips in surface temperature. In summary, planets may appear to have hot days and cold nights only for the time that it takes for heat to be transported from night to day side. In the process of studying the observed phase variations of transiting exoplanets, we can better understand their atmospheric compositions and analyze the potential climate scenarios of these alien worlds. Yuan & Astudillo-Delgado (2019) --- In this paper, I present a statistical correlation between the phase variations in infrared fluxes from transiting hot Jupiters and their atmospheric and transport properties. Using a multivariate linear regression model, I show how the phase variations could be used to determine the day-night termperature contrast of an unknown planet. I also conduct atmospheric circulation and energy transport simulations to better understand how the planet's various properties influence the infrared flux variations.

Semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) off protons and deuterons, A(e,e'p)X, has been investigated using measurements taken with the ep* detector at a four-momentum transfer squared, Q2, of 2.3 (GeV/c)2 and 0.64 (GeV/c)2, and the Electron Proton Elastic Scattering (EPE) process, ep* scattering, at a Q2 of 1.02 (GeV/c)2. These two datasets demonstrate the separation of various final state interaction effects in the A(e,e'p)X scattering process. Exchanges of two pions between the participating hadrons lead to a reduction in the measured cross section in the Deep Inelastic Process (DIP) region, as compared to the Cross Section for Elastic Electron Scattering (CS(e,e)) region on the same targets. The modelling of the FSI reduces the difference between the DIP and CS(e,e) cross sections. These final state interaction effects are dependent on the Four-Momentum Transfert, Q2, and the Bjorken x, xB, kinematic variables.

Quarkonia are bound states of heavy quark and antiquark. They provide an effective probe of the hot quark matter produced in heavy ion collision experiments. Measurements of quarkonium production and suppression serve as unique tests of the dynamics of thermalization and hadronization in such collisions. In this work, we present our predictions for the bottomonia and charmonia states' widths in a deconfined quark gluon plasma (QGP). Calculations are performed at second order in strong coupling constant alpha_s in large spacing approximation at finite temperatures. Our results show that all bound states except for the J/psi are significantly broadened in the deconfined matter. The relative widths of J/psi are much smaller than those of the other states. In string theory and field theory dualities, the gauge groups of special configurations of branes determine the low energy theories. For the case of four-dimensional N=4 supersymmetric Yang-Mills (SYM) theory, it was conjectured that a real gauge group leads to a complex conformal field theory (CFT), while a complex gauge group leads to a real CFT. Real and complex deformation of a CFT are a continuous family of theories connected by a geometric Weyl transformation. In the case of the N=4 SYM, it was found that there are two continuous families of real gauge groups, those with the SO(2) R-symmetry and with the ISO(2) R-symmetry. It was conjectured that the theories with the SO(2) R-symmetry lead to complex CFTs and those with the ISO(2) R-symmetry lead to real CFTs. In this paper, we test these conjectures using a large N limit of planar N=4 SYM. In particular, we argue that the theories with the ISO(2) R-symmetry have a different weak coupling limit from the theories with the SO(2) R-symmetry. We find the theories with the ISO(2) R-symmetry to have complex deformation, while the theories with the SO(2) R-symmetry have real deformation. We also make a case for the weak coupling limit of the real deformation of the theory with the ISO(2) R-symmetry, which involves the truncation of the beta-deformation to a particular complex symplectic form. We call this weak coupling limit of the real deformation of the theory with the ISO(2) R-symmetry real beta-deformation. We argue that the real beta-deformed theory has a geometry of a complex manifold with a holomorphic symplectic form. -- ''Michael Lashof (December, 2023)'' Real versus complex beta-deformation of the N=4 planar super Yang-Mills theory. One of the most widely used methods of measuring the distance to objects in the Universe is the technique of type Ia supernova supernovae. These events result from the explosion of dense stars, their light can be seen at large distances, therefore their spectra allow one to determine not only the type of supernova but also its brightness. The distance to which this method gives measured cosmological parameters is usually accepted with confidence. However, using this technique to measure the parameters of the Universe leads to systematic bias in the result. These conclusions are based on the assumption that all type Ia supernovae have the same peculiar velocities in the vicinity of the Local Supercluster, which was established using another method. We show that this hypothesis is incorrect, the type Ia supernovae have different peculiar velocities and this fact significantly changes the estimated values of the parameters of the Universe.

The dewetting of thin liquid films on solid surfaces is an interesting process due to its strong influences on heat and mass transfer, as well as surface chemistry. Because of this, dewetting has been studied for many years in both the academic and industrial arenas. Dewetting has been shown to be generically irreversible and governed by dynamical evolution equations for the height of the film and the contact angle at the edge of the droplet. When the contact line moves, it leaves a behind a thin "foot" of liquid, which can act to stabilize the drop by keeping it in equilibrium. However, if the contact line is slowed, and/or the fluid is not sufficiently viscous, the foot can thicken, and the drop can become unstable to further motions. In the first part of this study, we observed that for dewetting drops on hydrophobic surfaces, it was possible to stabilise the foot at constant volume (with variations in temperature and viscosity) via an oscillatory relaxation mode, which has previously been observed by other groups. Here we present experimental evidence for this relaxation mode, and explore its dependency on viscosity, temperature, and the fluid's contact angle.

Observing the gas temperature drop in the high-density nucleus of L 1544, Caselli et al. (2008) using the Heterodyne Instrument for the Infrared Imaging (HIFI) on board the *Herschel Space Observatory* revealed that the gas and dust are well coupled and the coldest emitting regions are close to the center. The obtained temperature maps showed a clear drop of the gas temperature from the outside in, which was not expected from previous temperature models. Moreover, the gas and dust are expected to be separated in the high density regions such as the central region of L 1544 since the dust grain temperature is regulated by the gas heating via photoelectric effect and rotational friction. These findings challenged the theories of early cloud formation and early cloud evolution. The central region of dense cores has been a topic of active research for decades. From infrared and radio observations, the central concentration of gas and dust is often found with radii of a few hundred AUs (astronomical units). The physical process responsible for the central concentration has been the subject of theoretical study for more than 40 years, yet there is still no general agreement on the origin of these very dense and cold regions. One ambipolar diffusion theory invokes the theory of a polar diffusion, namely the interaction between the charged particles (gas and electrons) and the neutral particles (dust and molecules). The charged particles form a dynamically active magnetized flow that exerts a force on the neutral particles. The neutral particles are therefore expected to move toward the central source in a flat disk-like configuration. In contrast, another theory based on thermal pressure predict that the central region is void. The heating is concentrated in the outer part of the core. The inner regions remain cold and can even become very unstable. The dust and gas have been found to be coupled in the high-density regions of L 1544, in conflict with the prediction of the ambipolar diffusion theory. Observations with *Herschel* showed that the dust and gas are well coupled and the coldest emitting regions are close to the center. This conclusion is contrary to the theoretical predictions of the ambipolar diffusion theory and suggests that another process must be at play.

In this paper, we present a detailed phenomenological study of high-transverse-momentum dijet production in proton-proton collisions at mid-rapidity at $\sqrt{s}=200$ GeV at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). Using the leading-order $k_t$-factorization approach based on the KS unintegrated gluon distribution function (UGDF), we compare to recent next-to-leading order calculations performed with the dipole gluon scattering amplitude in the color-glass- condensate formalism. We find that the next-to-leading order calculations describe the data better than the leading-order calculation, especially at large values of the proton-proton transverse momentum. The underlying assumption of the $k_t$-factorization approach is that the partonic subprocesses factorize at a sufficiently high virtuality of the subprocesses, i.e. the transverse momenta of the partons participating in the collision are large compared to the resolution scale of the $k_t$-factorization approach. The former allows one to express the cross section in a factorized form by convolution of off-shell parton distribution and fragmentation functions with the gluon density in the proton and the Mellin moment of the corresponding parton cross section. While this approach was shown to be very successful in predicting single hadroproduction processes, its extension to the description of dijet production is not straightforward. In the dijet cross section, two or more off-shell partons contribute at the leading order. The results of the Altarelli-Parisi evolution equations are far from perfect, since they involve multiple convolutions of off-shell parton distributions with dipole gluon scattering amplitudes. The dipoles are expanded in a series of orthogonal functions , which become gradually less and less orthogonal at a small resolution parameter. In the $k_t$-factorization approach, the off-shell partons are described by unintegrated gluon distributions, which provide a probabilistic interpretation of the transverse degrees of freedom. The latter are sums of (multi-) perturbative gluon ladders with negative probabilities. The recombination of these off-shell partons into color-singlet hadrons or jets is then modeled by a local parton-hadron duality with certain tunable gluon distributions.

nanopores made in thin films of mica have been shown to transduce differential ionic current magnitude as well as direction. When exposing mica to a polarized light source, periodically ordered domains with helical, radial and angular ordering have been observed. We use optical force microscopy to image nanopores in thin mica films with periodically ordered domains. We show that the ordering in the film is transferred to the nanopore which exhibits the same ordering. When using electric fields to transduce the current, the nanopore current magnitude and direction follows the ordering in the domain and film respectively. These periodic ordering schemes are only observed in narrow capillaries less than 100 nm in diameter. The underlying physical mechanism is due to nonlinear depolarizing Poole-Frenkel current flowing through the walls of the capillaries. The narrow width and anisotropic structural and electrical properties of these nanopores make them ideal systems for studying transport phenomena in the presence of ordering. This work was supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant No. ECCS-1709657.

Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m wormholes are solutions to the Einstein field equations relating to traversable geometries that may be used to transport objects from one location to another through what would otherwise be considered as an event horizon. It has been proposed that charged dust balls may be able to be transported through these wormholes, however due to the presence of the electric field that would be induced on the charged dust ball, it is expected that the energy-momentum of the dust ball will be lost due to radiation into space. Hence, it is concluded that it is not possible for a charged dust ball to be transported through a Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m wormhole. This article presents a method for the transportation of dust particles through traversable wormholes. It is shown that the electromagnetic field of a dust particle may increase the exit radius of a traversable wormhole but, because the energy-momentum of the dust is lost through radiation, the dust cannot be transported through the wormhole.

Neutrino oscillations reveal the presence of three light neutrino mass eigenstates with “active” masses of about 0.05 eV. These particles constitute most of the visible mass in the universe. Their properties and interactions with other particles are precisely measured by the experiments. A massive, as-yet-unseen state, would induce transitions between these eigenstates giving it a “sterile” neutrino state and thus accounting for the dominance of matter over anti-matter in the universe. The latter is known as the “baryogenesis” problem. Large extra dimensions (LEDs) provide a natural mechanism by which conservation laws may be localised in a four dimensional brane embedded in a higher dimensional space-time. The LEDs must be compact, in order to solve the conservation problem. The apparent violation of the conservation of energy in our universe, implied by the observed dilution of the cosmic microwave background (CMB), is explained by the creation of AdSLEDs in our universe on a brane embedded in an anti-de Sitter (AdS) LED with negative cosmological constant. In this scenario the universe is strictly four dimensional due to a fundamental conflict between the conservation of energy in our brane world and the continuous creation of AdSLEDs. In standard models of cosmology, the observed CMB temperature is generated by photons which are created after the decoupling of the free energy of the particles which comprise the CMB. The photons travel across the observable universe before reaching us. Therefore, the observed temperature of the CMB is the result of the sum of the energies of all the particles after they were created, before they were able to interact. If the universe is strictly four dimensional, with no additional space-time dimensions, then this conservation of energy is maintained, as all energy remains in the universe. However, if our universe is embedded in an AdSLED with negative cosmological constant, then this conservation of energy is violated, as AdSLEDs are created in order to alter the brane world dynamics.

By calculating the small-scale redshifted 21cm power spectrum, we can detect the unique HII region shapes imparted by quasars during reionization. The structure of these HII regions affects the 21cm signal, the faint, shifting signal of neutral hydrogen. We propose to use the 21cm small-scale redshifted power spectrum to detect the unique HII region shapes imparted by quasars during reionization. A precision measurement of the Casimir-Lifshitz force between a gold-plated sphere and a glass plate in water is presented. The experiments are performed at 25°C and at a pressure difference of 2.5 kPa, which is below the superheating pressure of water. The measured Casimir force is in good agreement with the theoretical prediction within the measurement uncertainty, which demonstrates the excellent performance of our experimental apparatus and methods. Our measurement improves the accuracy of previous experiments by a factor of 3-5, and is the first highly accurate measurement at pressures below the superheating pressure of water. Our results further confirm the universality of the Casimir force and the validity of the fluctuation theory of thermal physics at microscopic and macroscopic scales. The Casimir force is one of the most remarkable macroscopic quantum phenomena. It arises from the quantum electromagnetic fluctuations of the electromagnetic (EM) field. The EM field fluctuations between objects can cause objects with different shapes, sizes, and physical properties experience attractive or repulsive forces, depending on their relative geometries and material properties. The Casimir force was first measured between a gold-plated sphere and a glass plate in a laboratory in the late 1960s, which confirmed the theoretical prediction within a few percent accuracy. In the past few decades, experiments measuring the Casimir force have steadily improved in both precision and accuracy. By now, the Casimir force has been measured between a simple plate and a sphere, a plate and a cylinder, a sphere and a cylinder, two spheres, and two plane mirrors. The universality of the Casimir force has also been experimentally confirmed. A pressure difference of 2.5 kPa is measured at the superheating pressure of water (3.98 kPa). Water is a complex fluid that has a relatively high boiling point and low conductivity, and it is widely used in laboratories. In the present experiments, the Casimir apparatus is immersed in water to avoid heating effects caused by the water's high boiling point. Using a micromachined oscillator, a total noise level of 22.3 dB is obtained, and the effect of the residual thermal noise is suppressed to an unprecedentedly high level. The pressure difference is generated by the water's anisotropic thermal expansion caused by the temperature difference. By monitoring the cavity length using an interferometric technique, the Casimir force is demodulated and the output signal is used to calculate the Casimir force. Our experimental apparatus has excellent stability, which is demonstrated by the high repeatability of the measurements. To evaluate the accuracy of our measurement, we perform three types of cross validation. First, the residual thermal noise is eliminated by subtracting the average signal from the demodulated signal. Second, the thermal noise is eliminated by filtering the output signal from a stopped noise source. Third, the systematic errors are reduced by performing multiple measurements using the same configuration. Frequent pattern mining has been widely used for discovering interesting patterns in transactional databases. This work proposes to explore clustering of frequent patterns that appear in combination in a transactional database. Clustering of frequent patterns that appear together in a transactional database is further used to understand their relationship, e.g., spatial, temporal or semantic. In particular, this work focuses on mining maximal frequent patterns, which have not been considered before. This is significant as many real world frequently appearing patterns are found in transactional databases. Patterns appearing together are discovered using a novel technique based on co-occurrence analysis of maximal frequent patterns. The proposed technique is evaluated using real world transactional data from a telecommunication service provider. The discovered patterns are shown to be useful for performing online analytics for customer usage behavior. In this paper we study dynamical systems with holes. These are dynamical systems with non-empty domains on which the map is somehow constrained to behave in a certain way. For instance, a map may have two boundary points from which it is required to remain in the complement of the domain of the map. Another example is a flow that is divergence free and has a terminal condition that requires the flow to remain bounded. Examples of such dynamical systems arise frequently in various fields of science, including physics, biological modeling and chemistry. In the example of a map restricted to holes, the idea is that the dynamics on the holes is much faster than the dynamics in the domains where the holes are and, therefore, one might think of the holes as being empty. We refer to such systems as singular dynamical systems with holes. In this paper we show that, under mild assumptions, there always exists at least one physical measure for singular dynamical systems with holes. This physical measure is characterized in terms of convergence and non-convergence properties with respect to the domain of the map restricted to the holes. The main novelty of this paper is the introduction of a new method to prove the existence of a physical measure that uses the ergodic properties of the map restricted to the holes. This new method is inspired by that introduced in [1] by Baldi and Fisher to prove the existence of physical measures for compact systems with holes.

Evidence of dark matter annihilations in the WMAP data. WMAP (Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Measurement Program) is a spacecraft designed to study the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Since its launch in 2001, WMAP has made detailed observations of the CMB. One of WMAP's most interesting findings was the detection of the "haze" caused by emissions from dust clouds, our galaxy, and structures along the line of sight. Using data from WMAP's second and third temperature and polarization channels, combined with data from the Differential Microwave Radiometer's (DMR) first channel, scientists were able to more precisely measure the intensity of the CMB as a function of frequency. They found a sharp rise in intensity at a frequency of about 0.56 Hz, which is unexpected if the intensity is solely caused by the Galactic Haze. Inclusion of a signal from the dark matter component of the Galactic Haze only partially explains the excess intensity, indicating the presence of an additional contribution with different frequency and much smaller intensity relative to the Haze. This additional contribution is likely to be caused by dark matter annihilations.
